examples: The designer's ability was obvious from her portfolio.
The ability to work with others is a key requirement.

vocabulary.definition: to look for; to submit an application
examples: The college graduate applied for three jobs and received three offers.
Everyone who is interested should apply in person at any branch office.

vocabulary.definition: a person's experience, education, and family history
examples: Your background in the publishing industry is a definite asset for this job.
The employer did a complete background check before offering him the job.
Thanks to her careful research, the applicant felt that she was ready for the interview with the director of the program.
The employer wasn't ready for the applicant's questions.

vocabulary.definition: to ask to come; to beckon
examples: The young woman was so excited when she was called in for an interview that she told everyone she knew.
The human resources manager called in all the qualified applicants for a second interview.

vocabulary.definition: a belief in one's abilities, self-esteem
examples: Good applicants show confidence during an interview.
He had too much confidence and thought that the job was his.

vocabulary.definition: on a continual basis, happening all the time
examples: The company is constantly looking for highly trained employees.
Martin constantly checked his messages to see if anyone had called for an interview.
Our department head is an expert in financing.
The candidate demonstrated that he was an expert in marketing.

vocabulary.definition: v., to take additional steps, to continue; n., the continuation of a previous action
examples: Always follow up an interview with a thank-you note.
As a follow up, the candidate sent the company a list of references.
Marla was hesitant about negotiating a higher salary.
The recent college graduate was hesitant about accepting his first offer.

vocabulary.definition: to introduce; to show; to offer for consideration
examples: The human resources director presents each candidate's résumé to the department supervisor for review.
The candidate presented her qualifications so well that the employer offered her a job on the spot.
Her hands trembled and she spoke weakly at the interview.
She wrote so weakly we couldn't read it.
